findings.repro: There is a race between the delete and a concurrent insert. Two requests from the same org name one slip S. Request A is valid and is inside private.record_payment, holding the lease lock with its insert not yet committed. Request B fails early (another lease id giving 404, or a bad receivedAt giving 400), so the route calls cleanupRejectedSlip. removeOrphanSlip's `payments.findFirst({ slip_path })` cannot see A's uncommitted row, so B deletes S through the admin Storage client. Then A commits a payment whose slip_path points to an object that no longer exists. That breaks R44 ('slip_path must point to an existing file'), and getSlipUrl later returns 404. The window is small: it needs two requests naming the same slip at once with different outcomes. This change widens it by adding route-level cleanup on every pre-authorization failure.
findings.fix: Run the reference check and the delete under the same serialization that record_payment uses. One option is a plpgsql function that takes a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(slip_path))` (or locks the lease row when the lease is known) and record_payment takes the same lock before its storage.objects existence check. Another option is to delete only objects older than N seconds that have no payment, which a sweeper can handle. Add a concurrency test: one valid request and one failing request with the same slip, then assert the stored payment's slip still exists.

findings.repro: The open-redirect guard safeNextPath is untested. I traced by hand that '//evil.com', '/\\evil.com', '/\t/evil.com', 'https://evil.com' and 'javascript:...' all fall back to '/', and a curl probe of /payments/return shows the server encodes `next` correctly (307 to /login?next=%2Fpayments%2Freturn%3Fbill_id%3D...). Even so, nothing in tests/ imports safeNextPath, so a later edit could reopen the redirect without anyone noticing. Separately, lines 19-21 are dead code: the function has already checked `startsWith('/')`, so `firstSlash` is always 0 and `colon < firstSlash` can never be true.
findings.fix: Add tests/unit/safe-next-path.test.ts with a table of inputs: '//x', '/\\x', '/\tx', '/\n/x', 'http://x', 'javascript:alert(1)', '', undefined and ['/a','/b'] should all give '/', while '/payments/return?bill_id=…' should be kept. Delete the dead colon check, or replace it with a real check such as `new URL(next, 'http://local').origin === 'http://local'`.

findings.repro: When a POST fails inside recordPayment (bad receivedAt, 422 over the cap, a 409), the slip cleanup runs twice. recordPayment's own catch (payments.ts:154) runs removeOrphanSlip, and then the route's catch runs cleanupRejectedSlip, which reloads the caller, queries payments again and calls Storage remove again. This is not a correctness bug, but it doubles the DB and Storage round-trips on every failed request. It also leaves two cleanup paths that have to stay in sync, and the comment at payments.ts:110-111 already has to explain the duplication.
findings.fix: Use a single cleanup owner. Either have the route pass a flag, or move the pre-authorization into recordPayment through an option such as `opts.preAuthorized`. Another way is to let the route alone own cleanup and remove the catch from recordPayment for route callers, keeping the internal cleanup only for direct service callers (seed and actions).
